newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Oil, chemicals boost South African Jan imports.
newsitem.headline: Oil, chemicals boost South African Jan imports.

text.p: Sharply higher imports of mineral products, including crude oil, and chemical products contributed to a big jump in South African imports in January, according to Customs and Excise.
Imports of mineral products totalled 1,186.2 million rand, nearly the double the 646.8 million imported in same month last year, while chemical products rose to 1,262.1 million from 782.4 million.
The other notable category of import increase was machinery, which rose to 3,481.5 million rand from 2,684.2 million a year ago.
Several analysts were surprised by the high level of imports in January which totalled 10.7 billion rand against 8.5 billion in December 1996 and 8.3 billion in January 1996.
High imports largely offset the impact of a surge in exports to 11.3 billion rand in January from 10.5 in December and 7.4 billion a year ago.
As a result, the trade surplus came in at a somewhat disappointing 517.20 million rand against the Reuters consensus forecast of 817 million.
South African trade data covers the total foreign trade statistics of the common customs area of South Africa, Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia and Swaziland.
